question.text: What is the Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) tax rate on equity mutual fund units sold within 12 months of purchase (FY 2025-26)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Equity mutual fund units sold within 12 months of purchase are treated as Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG). Following the revision in Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 effective for transfers on or after 23 July 2024, STCG on listed equity and equity-oriented mutual funds is taxed at a flat 20% rate (raised from the earlier 15%). The 12-month holding period continues to be the boundary between short-term and long-term for equity-oriented schemes. The Trap: "15%" was the pre-July 2024 STCG rate and no longer applies for the current FY. "12.5%" is the LTCG rate (after 12 months) above the Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption — it applies to long-term gains, not short-term. "10%" was the older LTCG rate (above Rs. 1 lakh) before the revision. Note: The cited NISM Series V-B workbook pages (119-121) support the 12-month holding period and the application of new rates from 23 July 2024, but do not explicitly state the 20% STCG rate. The framing above reflects current Income Tax Act provisions as revised by Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024.
